question: In a Canadian anti-dumping or subsidy investigation, what are the distinct roles of the Canada Border Services Agency and the Canadian International Trade Tribunal?
generated_answer:
The Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and the Canadian International Trade Tribunal (CITT) are two separate organizations with distinct roles in the investigation of dumping and subsidizing complaints. You can find more information about the CBSA and the CITT on their respective websites. CBSA: www.cbsa-asfc.gc.ca
CITT: www.citt-tcce.gc.ca
The CBSA is responsible for conducting investigations into dumping and subsidizing complaints. The CBSA determines whether goods imported into Canada are being dumped or subsidized, and whether such dumping or subsidizing is causing injury or retardation or is threatening to cause injury to the Canadian industry. The CBSA also determines the margin of dumping or the amount of subsidy. The CITT is responsible for conducting inquiries into complaints of injury to the Canadian industry. The CITT determines whether dumped or subsidized goods are causing injury or retardation or are threatening to cause injury to the Canadian industry. The CITT also determines whether the dumping or subsidizing is a principal cause of the injury. The CITT may also recommend remedial measures to the Minister of Finance. The CBSA and the CITT work together to ensure that the investigation and inquiry are conducted in a fair and impartial manner. The CBSA and the CITT also work together to ensure that the investigation and inquiry are conducted in a timely manner. The CBSA and the CITT are committed to providing a high level of service to the Canadian industry and to ensuring that the investigation and inquiry are conducted in a fair and impartial manner.
